newsitem.title: USA: FERC proposes LILCO open lines to county.
newsitem.headline: FERC proposes LILCO open lines to county.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission has proposed that Long Island Lighting Co electric transmission lines be used to transmit power generated by outside sources.

The Suffolk County Electrical Agency sought the FERC ruling pursuant to the Federal Power Act, as amended by the Energy Power Act, to obtain transmission services that will allow its resale of lower-cost power from suppliers outside Long Island including Northeast Utilities and Enron Corp.
The proposal was made on December 31, 1996, FERC said.

The proposal would require LILCO to provide services that were available to its customers prior to and including October 24, the effective date of the Energy Power Act. FERC would also order further procedures to establish rates, terms and conditions of the services.
At the same time, LILCO protested FERC's proposal which it said violates several sections of the Federal Power Act.

LILCO contends the Suffolk request would accommodate a sham wholesale transaction, that it is not in the public interest and that it threatens to impair the reliability of its transmission and distribution systems.

In addition, LILCO also noted that a FERC ruling would be inconsistent with the Long Island Power Authority's exclusive authority under New York law to acquire and transform the utility into a publicly-owned entity.
A transmission order, LILCO contended, would achieve virtually the same result as a LIPA takeover.
